title: Combinatorial Polynomial-Time Algorithm for MIS/MWIS in Perfect Graphs
statement_text: No combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm is known for any of MIS, MWIS, MC, and MWC in perfect graphs; finding one is a major open problem in the field. At the moment we do not even have a polynomial-time combinatorial algorithm to solve MIS in perfect graphs with no hole of length four.
context_text: A hole is an induced cycle of length at least $4$, an antihole is the complement of one, and a hole or antihole is long if its length is at least $5$. MIS, MWIS, MC and MWC denote the Maximum (Weight) Independent Set and Maximum (Weight) Clique problems (weights are non-negative on vertices). All four problems are solvable in polynomial time on perfect graphs by the algorithm of Grötschel, Lovász and Schrijver, which however uses the ellipsoid method. The authors have no precise definition of a combinatorial algorithm (a good rule of thumb: an algorithm not using division), but roughly mean one described as a sequence of operations applied directly to the vertices and edges of the graph, without techniques such as the ellipsoid or simplex method. Besides MIS in $C_4$-free perfect graphs, another important special case is MC in perfect graphs with no long antihole, which by complementation is a special case of MIS in long-hole-free graphs; the latter was open when the paper was submitted and has since been solved in polynomial time by Abrishami, Chudnovsky and Pilipczuk, as the authors note. This is a long-standing community problem, not introduced by the authors.
notes: A long-standing community open problem cited as motivation in the introduction; not introduced by these authors. PDF source — math may be garbled.
paper_title: On the Maximum Weight Independent Set Problem in graphs without induced cycles of length at least five

title: FPT Algorithm for MWIS in (Long-Hole, k-Prism)-Free Graphs
statement_text: We do not see how to turn the $n^{O(k)}$-time algorithm for MWIS in (long-hole, $k$-prism)-free $n$-vertex graphs into an FPT-algorithm (parameterized by $k$), without using the result of Abrishami, Chudnovsky and Pilipczuk (polynomial-time MWIS in long-hole-free graphs).
context_text: A hole is an induced cycle of length at least $4$, an antihole is the complement of one, and a hole or antihole is long if its length is at least $5$. MIS, MWIS, MC and MWC denote the Maximum (Weight) Independent Set and Maximum (Weight) Clique problems (weights are non-negative on vertices). For an integer $k>0$, the $k$-prism is the graph on $\{a_1,\dots,a_k,b_1,\dots,b_k\}$ in which $\{a_1,\dots,a_k\}$ and $\{b_1,\dots,b_k\}$ are cliques, $a_ib_i$ is an edge for every $i$, and there are no other edges; it is long-hole-free but has exponentially many minimal separators. The authors prove, using the potential maximal cliques framework of Bouchitté and Todinca, that for every integer $k>0$ MWIS can be solved in time $n^{O(k)}$ on $n$-vertex graphs containing neither a long hole nor the $k$-prism as an induced subgraph (and deduce a subexponential algorithm for MWIS on all long-hole-free graphs). An FPT algorithm would run in time $f(k)\,n^{O(1)}$. The authors note that, after submission, Abrishami, Chudnovsky and Pilipczuk solved MWIS in polynomial time on all long-hole-free graphs (with a conceptually much more complicated algorithm), which in particular gives such a running time; the question is therefore only whether the simpler approach of this paper can be made FPT, and is not a genuine open problem about complexity.
notes: Implicit open question stated in prose without a labelled environment. PDF source — math may be garbled.
